title: Biased derivative sum and Fourier coefficients
statement:
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $0<p<1$, and let $f$ be a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube. Give each coordinate an independent sign with probability $p$ of being negative, and write $D_i f$ for the difference between the values of $f$ with coordinate $i$ set to $1$ and to $-1$, divided by $2$. Then
\[\sum_{i=1}^n \mathbb{E}[D_i f]=\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}} |S|(1-2p)^{\max(|S|-1,0)}\widehat f(S),\]
where $\widehat f(S)$ is the uniform Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $S$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
